Supplementary results · ICASSP 2027 submission

Assessing Generalisation in AI-Generated Music Detection

Angelos-Nikolaos Kanatas, David López-Ayala, Pablo Zinemanas, Martín Rocamora, Xavier Serra, Dmitry Bogdanov

Music Technology Group, Universitat Pompeu Fabra, Barcelona · BMAT Licensing, Barcelona

Every comparison behind the paper's two tables, disaggregated: each family exclusion, each generator, each training–test pair, each human-made pool, and both decision thresholds.

All values are recomputed from the saved per-recording scores of the fitted detectors; nothing was refitted for this page, and the paper's printed rows are reproduced within rounding before any table is written (Provenance). AUROC throughout, higher is better; a loss is AUROC with a family removed minus AUROC under the size-matched control. AB is ArtifactBench, FMC is FakeMusicCaps, M8K is MUSIC8K; detector names follow the paper's tables. Generated on UTC.

At a glance

Four views that the paper's tables compress into single numbers. Colours follow the paper's figure: fusion, spectral templates, fingerprint, trajectory readout, mean and attention pooling, retrained baselines.

How to read

  • Table 1 protocol. Pooled training on the other two target collections plus SONICS. A family is removed from fitting and development wherever it occurs; the control keeps it but subsamples generated recordings to the removal count within each collection and split. Both arms score the same target recordings of that family against the same target humans.
  • Six primary comparisons (Suno, Udio in ArtifactBench and Echoes; MusicGen in ArtifactBench and FakeMusicCaps) were selected first; the seven extension comparisons (Stable Audio, AudioLDM, DiffRhythm) were added afterwards.
  • Table 2 protocol. One training collection, one test collection; nine pairs enter the summary (SONICS targets excluded: bandwidth alone separates the classes there). MUSIC8K averages four source-trained models against the same 1,102 FakeMusicCaps humans.
  • Per-generator AUROC is that generator's recordings against all human-made recordings of the same target. Slices under 40 recordings are marked with a dagger; they are descriptive.

Scope and limits

  • Repeated control draws or repeated detector fits: every comparison rests on one fit per arm and one control draw. The intervals shown resample recordings with the fitted models fixed.
  • MusicDET and CoMoE on the seven extension comparisons: not run (MusicDET fits human-made recordings only, so a generated-family removal cannot change it; CoMoE was not launched). Released ArtifactNet per generator exists only where a per-recording export exists (ArtifactBench, Echoes, MUSIC8K).
  • An acoustic duplicate audit across collections; leakage control is by recorded identity, prompt and reference groups.
  • Any per-recording mechanism attribution. Decoder classes are annotations from public specifications; proprietary services are marked undisclosed.

Family exclusion, every comparison, every detector

Removed minus size-matched control AUROC on the withheld family, per comparison. Base is mean AUROC on the full target test set with no family excluded. Hover a cell for the removed and control values; switch the metric to see them directly. Intervals are 95% recording-bootstrap intervals conditional on the fitted models (2,000 draws), available for the nine systems the bootstrap covered.

lossgainn = generated recordings of the withheld family in the target; humans: ArtifactBench 860, Echoes 59, FakeMusicCaps 1,102

Producer scripts/companion_disaggregate.py, from the pooled-training score files behind Table 1 (six primary and seven extension comparisons, the parameter-matched control and the composition arms); the recorded fold results are reproduced to 1e-9 and the printed Table 1 rows within rounding.

Which generators each detector reads when every family is present

Pooled-base models (no family excluded), one target collection at a time: AUROC of each generator's recordings against all humans of that collection. Rows carry the family and the annotated decoder class. This is the descriptive map of where each detector succeeds and fails before any exclusion.

Same producer and score files as above, base conditions; CLAM from its per-recording scores under the paper's source-reference scoring policy, MusicDET and CoMoE from their per-recording exports. Their recorded family and generator metrics (660 rows) are reproduced from the same files.

Released ArtifactNet by generator, at its native input rate

The released ArtifactNet build, scored by us with native input where the collection is distributed above 16 kHz, on the paired subsets where both the native and the 16 kHz input exist. Its training mix contains several of the evaluated families, so it is printed in the paper and not ranked; this table shows where it succeeds and fails per generator.

Withheld generators, version by version

For one family exclusion, every generator of the withheld family in the target: AUROC with the family removed (large figure) and under the size-matched control (small figure). Provenance slices of one brand behave differently; the paper's Suno and Udio version readings come from this table.

Same producer. MusicDET and CoMoE have slices for the six primary comparisons only; every other detector covers all thirteen.

Decoder class on the pooled bases

Target humans against the target recordings of one annotated decoder class, per target and detector, with every family in the pool. Classes absent from a pool are the weakest for every detector (Riffusion is excluded from all pools; Echoes' loop-recombination service has no relative anywhere), so absence and mechanism are not separated here.

Annotations: output/analysis/codec_class_map.json and decoder_class_map_artifactbench.json (verified, likely or unknown per generator; see Inventory). Three-reader values reproduce the recorded decoder table exactly.

Cross-corpus transfer, pair by pair

Train on one collection, test on another. The nine pairs of the paper's summary are the four trainers against ArtifactBench, Echoes and FakeMusicCaps; SONICS-target cells are shown but flagged (bandwidth cue); MUSIC8K cells use the same FakeMusicCaps humans. Released checkpoints are evaluated from their own training pools. Switch to the carried false-alarm rate: the trainer's 5% human threshold moved unchanged to the target.

AUROC recomputed from the hash-checked publication score cells (publication_g75_cells.load_cells) and, for learned fusion, from its single-source export; printed Table 2 rows reproduced within rounding. Carried rates are read from the recorded metric producers rather than recomputed.

Strictly unseen: brand and decoder class both absent from the training collection

Each cross-corpus cell's generated recordings are split by whether the trainer collection contained the generator's brand and whether it contained its decoder class. The strict subset has neither; the disclosed variant further drops proprietary generators whose class cannot be known. Means are over the nine summary pairs (three for released checkpoints); a subset needs at least 20 recordings to score.

Per-cell strict subsets (n and AUROC)
Brands and decoder classes each training collection contains

Subset definitions follow scripts/cell_overlap_profile.py. An earlier independent recheck of eight systems is reproduced exactly for the six whose scores did not change; the trajectory and fixed-fusion rows use the final publication scores.

Every generator in every cross-corpus cell

Pick a training and a test collection: AUROC per generator against the cell's humans, with the seen-brand and seen-class flags used above.

Same producer. Released checkpoints appear under their own pools (MoM for CLAM; SONICS for Sofia-VAG and SpecTTTra).

MUSIC8K by generator

Six 2026 generator releases against the same 1,102 FakeMusicCaps humans, for each source-trained model. The paper's MUSIC8K column recombines these by recording count; the mean here weights the four trainers equally.

Source: notes/codex_audit_2026-09-20/generator_detail_20260923/per_source_generator.csv (native scope), produced by generator_detail_20260923.py from the publication scores.

Human pools at fixed generated scores

Each model scores the same 3,614 MUSIC8K generated recordings against one human pool at a time. The range is highest minus lowest AUROC over the pools outside the training collection, averaged over trainers; in-corpus pools are marked and excluded from the range.

pool of the training collection, excluded from the range

Source: the publication human-population sweep (producer scripts/human_population_sweep.py) and the learned-fusion pool file; the recorded mean ranges are reproduced.

Decision thresholds: carried and recalibrated

Six training-test pairs with at least 200 held-out target humans (Echoes targets excluded). Carried: the trainer's 5% order-statistic threshold applied unchanged. Recalibrated: the same rule on 200 target humans, which are then excluded from evaluation; both thresholds are evaluated on identical recordings within a system. Means balance trainers as in the paper's figure.

Source: the publication calibration comparison (producer scripts/calibration_method_comparison.py) and the learned-fusion calibration file.

Generator inventory

Every generated source in the four evaluation collections: recording count in the target set, the collection's own source label (for Echoes, the conditioning mode: TTA text-to-audio, ATA audio-to-audio), brand used for the overlap flags, annotated decoder class and the confidence of that annotation.

Counts from the corrected target rosters; classes and confidences from the class maps above.
